changelog.text:
## [0.7.0] - 2026-11-06

### Added

- Settings → Plugins → Installed lists plugins that were refused when they were first loaded (for example an Apps-menu label equal to one of Mumcord's own, or a manifest field used without its permission), with the reason and the time, until Mumcord is closed
- Camera room: while your camera is on, "Background: {name}" in the room bar (or "Background" in your own tile's ⋯ menu) changes your background on the fly (None, Blur Light or Strong, a built-in or your own image) without stopping the camera and without changing your saved default. Hovering or focusing another person's tile shows the resolution and codec it arrives in, such as "720p · AV1".
- While your camera is on, the tray icon shows a red camera badge, its tooltip says "Camera on" and its menu offers "Turn off camera". A global camera hotkey opens the camera preview when the camera is off and turns it off when it is on
- Camera sharing entry points: a camera button in the user panel next to mute and deafen and a "Turn on camera" entry in the Apps menu open the camera preview; while the camera is on, the button turns red and turns it off at once, "● Camera on" shows under your name and a red camera icon next to it in the channel tree (other people with their camera on get a camera icon there too), and screen readers hear "Your camera is on" / "Your camera is off". When camera sharing isn't possible, both are disabled and say why (no relay, relay too old or not allowing cameras, P2P mode without the relay, no client certificate, or not in a voice channel).
- New Settings → Camera tab: a live preview that only runs on this device and stops when you leave the page, your camera, send quality, mirrored self-view, default background, blur strength and effect quality, "Manage images" for your own background images, "Turn my camera off when my screen locks", and how you see other people's cameras (Always / When I open the room / Never, data saver, reduce motion). Settings → Voice & Audio → Hotkeys has a "Turn camera on / off" hotkey; a key already used by another shortcut shows a conflict there, and a warning shows when the camera hotkey can't be registered. The camera privacy text says that Mumcord can't stop someone from taking a screenshot with their operating system.
- Camera tile options: the ⋯ button on a camera tile (or Enter / Shift+F10 on a focused tile) offers "Pin for me" (P), "Show large" (F), "Hide {name}'s video" (H, the video is then not downloaded at all) and "Quality for me" (Auto, Data saver up to 15 fps, Best up to 720p · 30 fps); your own tile offers "Hide self-view". The tiles are one Tab stop: the arrow keys, Home and End move between them, and Escape leaves the large view.
- Cameras next to a screen share or watch party: while you watch a share or are in a watch party, that picture stays large and the cameras become a strip beside it or above it, or are hidden (then they aren't downloaded, and the header still says how many are on). Share or party, cameras and the camera controls form one card with a single header that names the share or party, shows its details and chips and the Beside / Above / Hidden switch; your own camera comes first in the strip, and there is no separate "Camera room" tab meanwhile. Mumcord remembers your choice. F on a camera in the strip shows it large in place of the shared picture until you press Escape, and when the share or party ends, the cameras go back to the room grid. The tiles in the strip have the same ⋯ options and keys as in the room, and "Show large" is one choice shared by the room and the strip.
- The camera room: when people in your voice channel turn on their cameras, they show above the chat in a grid of up to nine tiles (or Speaker, one large tile with the others below), each with the person's name, a microphone-off icon, a green frame while they talk and an "fps" badge on a weak connection. Your own camera shows as a mirrored self-view with "Live", which you can hide for yourself. Tiles say when a camera is joining, full, couldn't be joined or hidden by you ("Show video"), and the people without a camera are listed below. The room bar turns your camera off, pops the room out into its own window, goes full screen or closes the room to a "{n} cameras on · Open room" bar. Screen readers hear who turned a camera on or off.
- Turning your camera on starts with a preview that nobody else sees: pick the camera, a background (None, Blur, Light or Strong, or one of 18 built-in images made for Mumcord, from warm light waves and a neon gaming room to a model railway at night and an underwater base, or your own), see the effect load, and choose whether to keep the background for next time. Turn on camera waits until the camera is live and shows the reason if it can't start; Cancel or Esc turns the camera off again.
- New documents for plugin authors and users: the API 1.1 author guide, how the plugin security score is calculated (and what it cannot tell you), and the updated registry format. The privacy policy now covers plugin websites, relay plugin data and plugin sounds.
- The plugin update review shows a "What's new in <version>" link when the plugin author gave release notes for that version; it opens in your browser.
- The Apps menu now shows icons for "Share your screen" and "Watch together", and plugins without an icon get a coloured tile of their own, also in the side panel, dialogs, the media area, plugin details and the relay data card
- Plugins can add up to two items each to the Apps menu in the chat, under a "Plugins" group with the plugin's icon and name (more than eight go under "More plugins…"), and the same items show in the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) as "Plugin: Item". A plugin can grey an item out with a reason shown below it.
- Plugins built for API 1.1 can send game data to one person through the server's relay when the relay allows plugin data: up to 64 KB per message, end-to-end encrypted, behind voice, screen sharing and files. Without the relay, small messages still go through the Mumble server. Turning off "Let plugins use a server's relay" moves plugin data off the relay at once.
- The "No relay for plugin data" notice in a plugin activity's own window now has a "Details" button that brings the main window to the front and opens the installed plugins
- Settings → Plugins has a "Plugin data through the relay" card: the on/off switch, whether each of your servers' relays allows plugin data (and how fast), and per plugin a switch plus how much data it used this session. The game stage shows the same state as a chip: "Relay · end-to-end encrypted" or "Mumble connection · slower".
- Plugin game data for the whole channel now goes once through the server's relay as well, end-to-end encrypted and only to people who run the same plugin; when someone leaves, the key changes. People who are not connected to the relay still get small messages through the Mumble server.
- The plugin install prompt shows the security score with its biggest reasons and the full breakdown, lists every website a plugin talks to, says who wrote its own code, and asks for one tick when needed ("I understand", or "Install anyway" for high-risk plugins). It also says when a plugin can't be installed and why, when your safety setting blocks it, when it needs a newer Mumcord, and when the package scores higher than its listing
- Plugin cards in Browse and the Installed list show the security score chip for unofficial plugins, Browse says "Needs Mumcord X or newer" with Install disabled when no version runs yet, and Settings → Plugins has a "Plugin safety" switch ("Don't allow high-risk plugins") and "Plugin sounds" volume and mute, all findable in settings search.
- Plugin web pages can open in a dialog with the plugin's name, an "Unofficial" chip where it applies, a close button and a reminder that Mumcord never asks for passwords inside the frame; Esc closes it and Tab stays inside.
- Plugins with a side panel can show their page right of the chat in place of the member list, with a "⋯" menu (plugin details, close), a close button, a resize handle (drag, or arrow keys in 1 rem steps) and a width remembered per plugin; only one side panel is open at a time.
- Plugins built for API 1.1 can play short sounds from their package (`audio.play`, `audio.stop-all`), heard only by you: at most four at once across all plugins (a new one stops the oldest), 12 dB quieter while anyone talks, silent while you are deafened, and following the "Plugin sounds" volume and mute in Settings → Plugins.
- Plugin authors: API 1.1 adds `webview.set-status` (SDK `webview::set_status`) for a short plain-text status line under the plugin's side panel, such as "3 drawing · relay · Esc leaves the board": at most 80 characters, no markup, an empty text clears it, and at most 4 updates per second are shown (quicker ones are merged, the last one wins).
- Plugin installs and automatic updates are safer: a package with a bad signature, a download or manifest that doesn't match its listing, a revoked version or a website that breaks the rules can't be installed at all; plugins that need a tick before installing (high risk, own code and websites, first plugin from a repository) are refused without it; and an automatic update waits for you when it adds websites, raises the risk score by 10 points or more, moves to a worse risk band, or would make a plugin high risk while "Don't allow high-risk plugins" is on
- Settings → Plugins → Updates shows each waiting update's security score before and after, and says why it waits (new websites, the risk went up, the score went up, the safety setting, the score couldn't be worked out, or a newer Mumcord is needed). Review and update opens a review that marks new websites "New", warns when one is not on the plugin's own domain, and asks you to tick "I understand the risk went up and I still trust the author" before an update that makes a plugin high risk
- A plugin that needs a newer Mumcord is refused at install with "Needs Mumcord X.Y.0 or newer" and nothing is written to disk, and automatic updates never move a plugin to a version this Mumcord can't run; the update waits as "Update available after updating Mumcord".
- Plugin web content now carries a "Plugin content · <plugin>" tag (with "Unofficial" for unofficial plugins), a button to mute its sounds once it plays any, and stays silent while you are deafened. A page that stops responding for 3 seconds is removed with "<plugin> stopped responding" and a Reload button, Esc or F6 inside it always takes the keyboard back to Mumcord, and a plugin page can run on the stage as its own media tab. When Mumcord froze while a plugin's web content was open, Settings → Plugins → Diagnostics counts it and lets you turn that web content on again
- Plugin activities show in the media area with Mumcord's own header (who started it, how many are in the game, who made the plugin, an "Unofficial" chip and the connection), a Full screen button with a short "Esc to exit" banner, and "Leave <plugin>"; closing or minimising the media area keeps it as a mini bar at the top of the chat. "Pop out" moves an activity into a window of its own (with always on top and "Pop back in"); a deafen from before it opened still silences it. When a server's relay doesn't allow plugin data, the activity says so in a "No relay for plugin data on this server." banner with a Details button that opens the relay settings. People in your channel see "<name> started <plugin> · Join" at the top of the chat, with a clear message when the activity is full or has ended, and for official plugins they don't have yet "<name> is playing <plugin> · Get plugin", which opens the normal install prompt. A plugin that tries to start a fourth activity in a channel shows "Too many activities in this channel"
- When more than one thing runs in the media area (a watched screen share, the watch party, a plugin activity), a row of tabs above it switches between them with a click, the arrow keys or Alt+1 … Alt+9. Switching never stops anything, and something new appears as a tab with a dot instead of taking over the picture you are watching
- The plugin SDK has a `1.1` feature that binds API 1.1 with typed wrappers for the stage, the Apps menu, the relay, sound effects, file save and picture import, posting an image to chat and the new webview places; 1.0 stays the default.
- Plugins can send typed messages to other players as Bovnar documents with the SDK's `bovnar` module (feature `1.1`): size limits are checked before sending and bad incoming data is dropped with a clear reason. The SDK bundles a prebuilt Bovnar 2.0.0 library for plugins, so plugin authors need no C compiler (#400)
- Plugin web pages are locked down harder: they can reach only the websites the plugin declares and you approved, never load scripts from them, can't use the camera, microphone, location, clipboard, full screen or other device features, can't start downloads, and can't open connections behind the scenes (link preconnect and WebRTC are switched off; on Windows all web traffic goes through a local filter that lets only approved websites and the chat's video and music players through). A plugin can show up to three pages at once: one in the stage, one in the side panel and one in its dialog or popover
- Plugins from repositories you added can show their own web pages too, if they are built for plugin API 1.1 and you allow it; they show only in the places the plugin lists. A plugin's side panel opens only right after you click something of that plugin, and only one plugin's side panel is open at a time
- On macOS, plugin web pages run in a view of their own next to Mumcord's window content, so a busy plugin page can no longer freeze the app; a page that stops responding is closed with "Reload" while everything else keeps working, and its "Plugin content" tag and mute button sit in a bar below the page
- A plugin web page that makes Mumcord's window stop responding for 5 seconds no longer leaves it frozen: Mumcord restarts the window while voice keeps running, turns that plugin's web content off until you turn it on again in Settings → Plugins, and notes it in the plugin's Diagnostics. Plugin pages can play sound only after you click inside them, Escape or F6 always takes keyboard focus back to Mumcord, and each page reports a heartbeat so a stuck page can be removed
- Plugin details pages list the websites a plugin talks to (with what it asked them for and today's request counts), where it shows, its own code and relay data, and show the security score card with the full breakdown.
- A "Which app's sound?" dialog opens while you share a window and Mumcord needs to know whose sound to share: pick an app that plays sound right now or "No sound"; the list updates while the dialog is open
- The Sound switch in the screen share dialog and in Settings → Screen sharing is now shown on every system, with a line saying what is shared (whole screen: desktop sound without Mumcord; one window: only that app's sound). Where sound cannot be shared, the switch is off and disabled with a note: "No sound: needs Windows 10 version 2004 or newer", "…macOS 13 or newer" or "…PipeWire" (#435)
- The live bar of your screen share says what its sound carries ("Sound: desktop", "Sound: Firefox") or "No sound" with the reason in a tooltip that screen readers read as well (#435)
- Screen sharing can include sound: sharing a whole screen shares all sound except Mumcord's own, sharing a window shares that app's sound. Works on Windows 10 (2004+), macOS 13+ and Linux with PipeWire; where it is unclear which app you mean (always on Wayland), Mumcord asks "Which app's sound?". There is no sound without PipeWire or on older systems.
- Bots are shown apart from people (#458): a new "Bots on this server" section below the channel tree lists every bot with what it does (e.g. Relay · Chat history · Webhooks), and its profile and menu, private messages included, work from there. Bots that never talk, like the relay, no longer appear in the channel tree, the member list, @mention suggestions or people pickers; bots with voice, like a music bot, stay in their channel. Bots carry a BOT badge instead of the Mumcord badge
- Settings → Screen sharing has an "Ask for these settings each time I share" switch and shows whether this computer plays AV1 and VP9 with hardware or software
- Kick… and Ban… in the Admin ▸ sub-menu of a person (issue #253): the kick dialog asks with the reason, the ban dialog with the reason, the length (1 hour, 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, permanent, a custom date), the targets (certificate and IP address with its mask, the address stays because a standard server matches it) and "Remove from server now". A precise ban adds one entry to the server's ban list with the safe save and then removes the person; a server that will not show its list only allows its own default length, and the dialog says so. The items show only with the Kick or Ban right on the root channel, never for yourself, and a refusal appears inside the open dialog.
- The server menu shows "Ban list…" when the server grants Ban on the root channel. The window lists the server's bans with name, certificate fingerprint, IP address or range, reason, since and end (permanent, a date, or expired), with search, an All/Active/Expired filter and sortable columns. An entry is edited in place (reason and end) or unbanned, a ban can be added for someone who is not online, and the changes are collected and saved together after reading the server's list again. Fingerprints are shortened and addresses masked by default, and nothing of the list is written to disk (#254)
- The picture of a watched screen share or watch party can be made taller or smaller: drag the handle between the picture and the chat, or focus it and use the arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home and End. It snaps at a third, half and two thirds, Enter or a double-click goes back to the original size, dragging it all the way up minimises it to the mini bar, and the height is remembered (#386)
- Mumcord respects what a server's relay allows: if the relay owner turned off images, files or screen sharing, that feature no longer goes through the relay. Screen sharing still works over a direct connection, and full-size images use a direct connection or the Mumble server instead
- Screen sharing picks its encoder automatically: Mumcord checks in the background which graphics-card encoders work and how well the processor handles AV1, then uses AV1 on the graphics card, AV1 on the processor (up to 1080p30, not on battery), or VP9. The check runs again after a driver or Mumcord update
- Sharing your screen first opens a short dialog: pick the resolution, frame rate, what to optimize for (balanced, sharp text or smooth motion), the codec and an upload limit, and see right away what viewers get and whether the share goes once through the relay or as one copy per viewer. "Use these settings next time" keeps the picks as your defaults
- Watching a screen share plays AV1 as well as VP9, decoded by the system where it can and by Mumcord itself otherwise, so AV1 shares play on every computer. Viewers can lower the frame rate they receive (Auto, up to 30 or up to 15) without the sharer encoding anything extra
- A screen share switches to VP9 while someone watches with an older Mumcord that can only play VP9, and goes back once they leave. If AV1 on the processor can't keep up, the share switches to VP9 by itself, and you can undo that once per share
- New "Screen sharing" tab in Settings: choose the default resolution, frame rate, what to optimise for, upload limit and codec (Auto, AV1 or VP9), turn graphics-card encoding on or off, see which encoder your computer uses and check again
- While you share your screen, the bar shows the quality, the encoder ("AV1 · hardware", "VP9 · CPU" …) and whether the share goes through the relay. A Quality menu changes resolution, frame rate and "Optimize for" within a second without restarting the share, the bar says when and why quality was lowered or a viewer needed VP9, and a notice explains an automatic switch to VP9 with Undo and Details
- The screen share viewer list shows each viewer's received quality, codec, path (relay broadcast, relay or direct) and a "Slow connection" badge, and a viewer's header shows the codec and path (for example "AV1 · via relay") with a Quality menu to cap the frame rate
- When a screen share can't go through the relay once for everyone, a notice says why and that each viewer gets their own copy (up to 8), with Got it. The viewer list shows the real limit of the running share, and the Quality menu shows the quality picked for this share, also when it was chosen only in the start dialog
- The server info panel lists what the relay allows ("Relay allows: Images · Files · Screen sharing"), and buttons and the image viewer say so in plain words when the relay doesn't allow a feature.
- Settings → Privacy & Connections has a new "File sharing" card: turn receiving files on or off, pick the maximum file size (100 MB to 2 GB) and choose the folder where received files are saved (by default a "Mumcord" folder inside Downloads).
- The message input has a paperclip button and accepts dropped files and folders in channels: each becomes a chip with its size or progress and a remove button. The paperclip says why it is unavailable when the server has no relay, the relay doesn't allow files, you have no certificate, or your peer-to-peer setting needs the relay.
- Dropping images into a channel asks whether to send them as images or share them as files; other files are shared at once. Private chats keep sending dropped images inline.
- Files shared in a channel show up as a file card with name, size, type and checksum. Every download asks first, programs and scripts get an extra warning before download and before opening, and the card shows the queue position, progress, the check that the file arrived unchanged, and Open / Open folder. Your own shared files show who downloaded them and a Stop sharing button (with a clear message if stopping fails)
- Plugins that talk to websites can only reach the websites they declared, on the exact address and port, and only at public internet addresses with a valid certificate; anything else is blocked, and each plugin's requests and blocked attempts are counted per day
- Plugin authors: `mumcord-plugin build` writes the manifest's `api` from the plugin API the plugin is built with and packs a `sounds/` folder; `mumcord-plugin check` fails when `api` doesn't match the plugin's imports and warns about a deprecated API
- Plugins can save a file, open a picture and post an image to chat, each only right after you click in the plugin and only with its permission: Mumcord's own save dialog and picker open, the plugin never learns where files are, pictures must be PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 10 MB, and an image too large for the server is shared as a file instead
- Plugin registries: `mumcord-plugin site-data` and `serve-registry` publish two indexes, `v1/index.json` with only API 1.0 versions for Mumcord 0.6 and `v1.1/index.json` (format 2) with every version, plus `v1.1/permissions.json`; registry version files accept `api = "1.1"`, `min_mumcord` and `origins`
- Plugin update review: "Skip this version" hides that version (a newer one is offered again), and the review shows the points each new permission adds and the recent-change points of the score.
- Screen sharing through the relay: when the server's relay offers it, your share is uploaded once and the relay sends it to every viewer, so up to the relay's limit (25 by default) can watch without costing you more upload. The picture is end-to-end encrypted, so the relay can't see it, and viewers who stop watching can't read what comes after. Viewers on older Mumcord versions still get their own copy, and if the relay goes away during a share, the first 8 viewers continue on their own copies without interruption
- A real click or key press inside a plugin's own web page now counts as a user gesture for that plugin, so it can open its side panel, dialog or activity, save a file or post to chat right after you click in its page. Clicks or key presses that the page fakes never count.
- Six built-in camera background images (Soft light, Library, Mountains, Studio, Night city, Beach) ship with the app for camera sharing's background effects; the privacy policy gains a camera section
- The latency card in Settings → Audio and in the connection panel now says why the time is longer than low-latency mode asks for: when the sound server runs with blocks larger than the buffer Mumcord requested because another application needs them, the card names the block and says Mumcord cannot make it smaller. This is Linux only, where one sound server graph serves every application.

### Changed

- An older Mumcord can now open a profile that a newer Mumcord already used, as long as the newer version only added things: your servers, history, identities and settings work, and the newer version later finds its own data unchanged. Settings the older version does not know are kept as they are. When a newer version changed the profile in a way an older one cannot handle, the "made by a newer Mumcord" message now also offers to roll the profile back to your version: Mumcord saves a full backup copy of the profile next to it, undoes only what the newer versions added (that data is lost, everything from your version stays) and starts normally. If the rollback fails, the profile stays exactly as it was. Profiles whose newer changes cannot be undone safely still offer only Download and Quit.
- The third-party notices (About → Licences) name the exact Bovnar release and upstream commit the app is built from (Bovnar 2.0.2). The notices are only generated when every file of the Bovnar crate matches the provenance manifest it ships, so the library in the app and its licence notices are tied to one upstream release
- Catching up on a channel's history with other Mumcord 0.7.0 users is much smaller and faster when it has pictures: each picture travels once, as itself, instead of inside every message, and pictures you already have are not downloaded again. Until a picture arrives its message shows a box of the right size; if it cannot be loaded the box says so, and with "Load full-size images from others" off it offers "Load image". Pictures from locked channels still only reach people inside them, and older Mumcord versions keep getting the full messages as before (#402)
- The diagnostic file (Settings → Advanced & Developer → Save diagnostic file) is now a Bovnar document: the same facts as before, still readable in any text editor, in a structured form (#400)

### Fixed

- After clicking inside a plugin's page, Escape or F6 now really moves the keyboard back to Mumcord: Tab and Shift+Tab used to keep moving inside the page
- Voice control can pick a plugin's tab in the media area by what it shows ("Test Stage Plugin"): the visible text is now part of the tab's accessible name
- Going back from a plugin's details in Settings → Plugins → Browse puts the keyboard focus back on that plugin in the list instead of losing it
- With "Show cameras: Always", the camera room opens again when the first camera in your channel turns on; it could stay closed behind "{n} cameras on · Open room" when the room had been opened before any camera was on
- The camera room now follows Settings → Camera: "Mirror my self-view" and "Reduce motion" (System, On or Off) take effect in the room and the strip; before, the self-view was always mirrored and the app's Reduce motion switch did nothing
- When a screen share you watch ends, its empty picture no longer stays behind: the media area goes back to what else is open, and cameras shown as a strip next to it return to the camera room grid
- When your camera stops by itself (the relay can't be reached, the camera is unplugged or taken by another app, or the server's relay ends it), Mumcord now says why: "Camera stopped: …" shows in the camera room bar, or below the camera bar above the chat when the room is closed, and screen readers read it. Dismiss hides it; turning the camera on again clears it
- Camera room: when someone turned on their camera, your picture of it no longer took 10 seconds or more to appear (or stayed at "Joining …"); the room no longer left and re-joined the camera while it came into view.
- Security: a plugin can no longer open its web dialog on its own. Like the side panel, it now opens only within 8 seconds after you click or type something for that plugin, and only once per click; a new page in a dialog that is already open still works
- A plugin's first messages to the channel through the relay (for example the first strokes on the Whiteboard) were lost while the relay connection was being set up, even though the plugin was told they were sent. They now wait briefly and arrive once the connection is up, also for people who join right then; if they cannot be delivered, the plugin gets an error instead
- Ctrl+C on selected chat text could leave the clipboard empty on Linux (X11): the web engine and the app both took the clipboard at once, and the app could then drop the text it had just been given. Ctrl+C now copies through the app alone, like the right-click Copy (#114)
- Messages from a plugin's web page now reach the plugin in the order the page sent them; two quick messages could arrive swapped, so a plugin could act on stale information
- Closing a plugin's web dialog with Esc or ✕ now ends the whole dialog: it could come back as an empty dialog a moment later and cover the app. Focus also returns to the button that opened the dialog instead of getting lost
- The plugin install prompt no longer warns that a repository is one you added once you have already installed a plugin from it
- Settings → Plugins → Installed shows the security score chip of developer plugins (for information only), and keeps showing an unofficial plugin's chip after it was updated
- Turning off a plugin's "may use the relay" switch now tells the plugin right away that the relay is switched off; before, it was not told and kept showing the relay as available. Its small messages still go through the Mumble server as when the relay is switched off for all plugins, instead of being refused
- After someone reconnected, the first relay messages a plugin sent to them directly could be dropped as repeats and never arrived; they now arrive
- After a reconnect, plugins sometimes never learned that the people in the channel run them too (for example when the voice server came back a moment after the others' announcements), so their messages to them were refused; they now learn it once both are back
- Settings → Plugins → Diagnostics now says why a plugin was refused at load, for example "an Apps-menu label is the same as one of Mumcord's own", instead of showing nothing.
- A plugin that talks to websites could not reach them right after it was installed, updated or loaded from a developer folder: its requests were refused until Mumcord was restarted
- Plugin SDK: a Bovnar document with one text of 64 KB or more is now refused as `too-large` instead of `malformed`, so plugins can tell the player the message is too big.
- The screen-share live bar keeps its buttons on one row when the chat is narrow (small window or members panel open): they show only their icons there, with their names as tooltips and for screen readers
- Apps without an icon of their own in "Which app's sound?" now get a square in the colours of the design instead of a random colour
- Audio no longer stutters when another application plays sound at the same time. The sound server delivers audio in blocks as large as the biggest block any application asks for, which can be much larger than the small buffer Mumcord requests, and the output queue was allowed to be smaller than one of those blocks: the part it could not fill stayed silent, and that is the stutter. The output queue now always covers one delivered block plus headroom, so the sound stays even. A larger block still means more delay, which no client can take back from the sound server, and the latency figure shows it honestly now; a change of the delivered block size is logged so a report can be read as the sound server rather than a broken device.
- Log lines from the very start of the app, such as the screen-share encoder check on older CPUs, are no longer missing from the log file and the diagnostic file
- A chat message from someone who leaves right after sending it (a shared file, too) now shows their name instead of an empty sender, and a block still applies to it.
- A screen share sent with VP9 no longer risks crashing Mumcord when the shared window grows or the quality steps up to a size larger than the one the share started at; the encoder now restarts at the new size with a fresh keyframe.
- Mumcord no longer crashes at start-up on older x86 processors without AVX2 (for example AMD FX or Intel Core of the Sandy and Ivy Bridge generations). The AV1 encoder that screen sharing tests at start-up crashed on these processors; screen sharing now uses VP9 there. If the AV1 test ever ends the app, the next start counts it as failed and does not run it again.
- Screen share sound polish (#435): the "Which app's sound?" list shows each app's own icon on Linux (a coloured square where the app has none), the live bar's sound line says "The Sound switch is off" or "“No sound” was chosen for this window" correctly instead of mixing the two up, the disabled Sound button names the real reason, and the speaker icons are drawn as outlines as in the design
- Opening a profile that a newer Mumcord already upgraded no longer ends start-up with a bare error: Mumcord now explains that the profile is from a newer version, shows both profile versions and offers "Download the latest version" and "Quit". The profile is left exactly as it is (#510)
- Kick… and Ban… in the Admin ▸ sub-menu of a person now open their dialog when clicked with the mouse; the click used to close the menu before it reached the item, so nothing happened (#507)
- The download confirmation no longer lets you press Download before it shows the folder the file will be saved to
- Joining a screen share no longer picks up the relay access meant for another broadcast of the same person (such as a camera or plugin data), so watching works while they share several things at once
- If you are not registered on a server whose relay only serves registered users, file sharing and other relay features now say "This server's relay is only available to registered users. Register on this server to use it." instead of claiming the relay could not be reached (#406)
- Switches stay visible in high-contrast (forced-colours) mode: the knob and track are drawn in system colours, and on and off differ by shape as well as col
- Screen sharing now speaks your language: the share dialog, the live bar with its quality menu, the viewer list, the stream viewer, the encoder and relay notices and the media area resize hints were still shown in English in all languages other than English.
- Starting a watch party or adding a video from the Apps menu no longer reloads the app when you confirm the link
- A mumbot shows as "Mumbot <version>" in the profile preview and the connection details instead of "Mumcord <version>", from what it announces about itself; older mumbots get the same label from their name and version (#459)
- A middle click on a link, or a click with Ctrl, Cmd or Shift held, opens it in your browser like a normal click. It used to load the page inside Mumcord, in a window of its own or in place of the whole app, and no page from outside ever gets a Mumcord window now (#418)
- A chat message you send now stays in the right time order: a message someone else wrote while yours was being sent no longer ends up above yours, before or after a restart
- Chat history of locked channels (password or restricted entry) is no longer shared with people who only follow or listen to them: only people inside the channel get its earlier messages, and members who use a channel password must prove they know the current one. "Follow all" now skips channels you may not enter. Older Mumcord versions still share it, so everyone should update (#382)
- When someone connects to you through the relay without sharing their network address ("Always use relay"), Mumcord no longer sends them yours either; the connection always went through the relay, so your address was revealed for nothing
- The letter shown in place of a missing plugin icon in Settings → Plugins → Installed now reads well on its tile: the tile uses checked theme colours, so the letter meets WCAG AA in the dark and light themes and with any accent colour (#405)
- The third-party notices (About → Licences) describe the bundled Bovnar C library correctly: it is compiled from the published bovnar crate on crates.io, pinned in Cargo.lock, not from a Mumcord fork pinned to a commit

### Internal

- Release and CI builds of the app run with `--locked`: the shipped binary is built from exactly the dependencies in Cargo.lock, the ones the third-party notices were generated from, or the build fails
- File offers and the file-sharing messages between Mumcord clients use the Bovnar data format through a pinned build of the Bovnar library; the plain line that official Mumble clients and older Mumcord versions see is unchanged, and the licences window lists Bovnar (#400)
- File transfer over the relay (not yet visible in the app): files travel only through the relay on their own stream with a size check, and a screen share or full-size image download continues when that switches the connection from direct to the relay
- Build scripts and cached CI steps for the AV1 screen-sharing libraries (SVT-AV1 encoder, dav1d decoder, and the NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and VA-API interfaces for graphics-card encoders); the licences window and third-party notices list them with their licence texts
- The file transfer stall test no longer pauses the sending client's process: a frozen client also stops sending to the Mumble server, whose own 30 s idle timeout can win the race on a loaded CI runner and shows the other failure text. A new debug-only hook `MUMCORD_TEST_FILE_STALL_AFTER` stops file bytes only, so the client's own 30 s stall timer decides the test (#420)
